clue.text: Hear out visiting minister's political aide, maybe

indicators.note: something visiting a place goes inside it, so the scrambled letters sit within the aide

parts.note: a PPS is a Parliamentary Private Secretary, a British minister's aide in the Commons

indicators.note: out here means disordered or put out of shape, signalling these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be heard by a minister's assistant, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the first word and 'visiting' puts it inside a Parliamentary Private Secretary, an MP who assists a UK government minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs of possibility, interchangeable in a sentence such as 'it may rain, possibly'.

clue.text: Some start celebrating upcoming Greek play

indicators.note: in a down clue upcoming means coming up the grid, read bottom to top
some of the words means a run of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: A troupe gets ready to celebrate an approaching Greek drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ARTCELE from 'start celebrating', and 'upcoming' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles and Euripides both wrote tragedies of this name about Agamemnon's daughter.

clue.text: Landlord, one that's found in bed

parts.note: a landlord of a pub or inn is the host
a means one, as in 'a dog'

explanation.surface: A landlord discovers someone in a guest's bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a flower bed, not one to sleep in.
explanation.definitionFit: This leafy perennial plant is a garden favourite, grown in flower beds and borders.

clue.text: Stanhope, minus front, rebuilt as another carriage

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put back together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
minus front means losing the first letter

explanation.surface: A Stanhope carriage, damaged at the front, is rebuilt as a new model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minus front' drops S from STANHOPE, and 'rebuilt' rearranges TANHOPE. A stanhope is itself a light carriage, hence 'another'.
explanation.definitionFit: A phaeton is a light, open, four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle.

clue.text: Text manager providing rocks for building

parts.note: an editor manages text; ED is the usual abbreviation for editor
providing as a conjunction means if, on condition that
rocks and ice are both slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: An editor is offered jewels in return for a construction deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' and 'ice' are both slang for diamonds, which is how one stands for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposing building or large structure is called an edifice; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: No strong drink served up as Guardian spirit

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means presented upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: mead is an alcoholic drink of fermented honey

explanation.surface: A paper's mascot laments that no liquor is on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses NO MEAD. 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper but just means protective.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek belief a daemon was an attendant spirit watching over a person.

clue.text: Novel finally edited, introducing knight and horse

indicators.note: edited text is changed and reorganised, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A novel's final draft brings in a knight on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' rearranges FINALLY with N and H. 'finally' is fodder, not a last-letter signal.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cleland's notorious 1748 erotic book is a novel.

clue.text: River sustaining sect's traditional way of life

indicators.note: in a down clue the river sustains, holding up from below, what comes above it

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A river supports a religious group's age-old customs.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'sustaining' puts URE underneath CULT.
explanation.definitionFit: Culture is the customs, arts and beliefs of a people, its inherited way of living.

clue.text: My tyres burst under ice — whodunnit?

indicators.note: in a down entry, under places this part below the other

parts.note: ice is slang for kill

indicators.note: burst tyres are broken apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puncture on an icy road prompts the question of who did it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ice' looks like the road hazard but is slang for kill. 'burst' turns MY TYRES into MYSTERY, which goes under MURDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunnit is a detective story where the reader tries to guess the killer.

clue.text: God and Eden's downfall rejected

indicators.note: rejected suggests being turned back, so the name is read from end to start

parts.note: the 1956 Suez Crisis brought down British Prime Minister Anthony Eden

explanation.surface: A religious reading: God and the fall from the Garden of Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the Garden of Eden, but this is Anthony Eden, the UK prime minister who resigned after the 1956 Suez Crisis; 'rejected' reads SUEZ backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief deity of the Greek pantheon, ruler of Olympus, is a god.

clue.text: A pretty old invader, one of four in VW?

parts.note: pretty and cute are synonyms for attractive
the Angles were a Germanic people who invaded Britain after the Romans left

explanation.surface: A sweet ancient raider turns out to belong in a Volkswagen.
explanation.walkthrough: VW looks like the car maker, but it is the two letters V and W: V has one sharp point and W has three, four in all.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle under ninety degrees is the kind found at the points of the letters V and W, which have four between them.

clue.text: Sound's singular feature

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a feature or characteristic is a trait

explanation.surface: A remark that one sound has a unique quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is a body of water here, not a noise; the 's after it means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow channel of sea between two landmasses, a synonym for a strait.

clue.text: Fan of wine, he and Bill may get indissolubly lashed

indicators.note: lashed is slang for drunk, and drunken letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of the word bill join the answer in the jumble

explanation.surface: A tipsy pair, a man and his friend Bill, inseparably drunk on wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lashed' (drunk) signals a composite anagram: the letters of 'he' (the answer) plus BILL rearrange to INDISSOLUBLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of wine and revelry is fairly called a lover of the grape.

clue.text: She foresaw Conservative fool with gunmen

parts.note: an ass is a fool
with and and both mean together with
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: A prophetess predicted a Tory idiot would turn up with armed men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gunmen' suggests criminals, but it means the gunners of the Royal Artillery, RA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan prophetess was given foresight but cursed never to be believed.

clue.text: Veronica did a 22 in balloon

indicators.note: in places the act of urinating inside the word for balloon

parts.note: to balloon is to swell
22 down is a wee-wee, so doing one means urinated

explanation.surface: A woman called Veronica relieved herself in a hot-air balloon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veronica' looks like a woman's name but is the botanical name of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is the genus name of this small blue-flowered plant.

clue.text: Warning about wrong packaging

indicators.note: packaging wraps round its contents, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a wrong is a sin
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A caution concerning faulty wrapping on goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a loud alarm device that sounds an alert, a warning signal.

clue.text: Angel's using drugs kept in heavy case

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the short word sits between the outer letters
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: on, as in 'on drugs', means using them
E is slang for ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: Someone called Angel is a drug user caught with a weighty bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angel's' reads as a possessive name but means 'Angel is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel and honey are both terms of endearment for a loved one, used the same way as 'darling'.

clue.text: Open University charged very big boss of Sky

parts.note: charged as in rushed forward, ran
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A university bills a top executive at Sky, the TV company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky' suggests the British broadcaster, but this is the Greek god of the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this primordial god personified the heavens and ruled them.

clue.text: Play golf with Olympian, getting thrashed

indicators.note: thrashed letters are beaten about and so rearranged

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A round of golf with an Olympic athlete who wins easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb with golf, but it is the definition: a George Bernard Shaw play.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1913 drama by George Bernard Shaw, the basis of My Fair Lady, is a stage play.

clue.text: Repairman keeps a snake

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the fixer holds the letter

parts.note: a mender is someone who repairs things

explanation.surface: A handyman keeps a pet serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snake' is the verb, to wind about, not the reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: To snake is to wind or wander along a twisting course, as a river does.

clue.text: Crude film that's about a sailor

parts.note: crude is unrefined oil
a film is a thin layer, a skin

explanation.surface: A vulgar movie featuring a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude film' suggests a rude movie; 'about a sailor' means worn round one.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof garment of oiled cloth is worn wrapped around a seaman.

clue.text: Nancy's repeated consent by phone to get rid of waste

indicators.note: repeated means the French yes is said a second time
Nancy is a French city, so the agreement is given in French and then heard
by phone means heard spoken, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: consent in French is oui, yes

explanation.surface: Someone named Nancy keeps agreeing on the phone to a rubbish collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nancy' is a woman's name in the surface but the French city, which makes the consent French.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's word for urinating, ridding the body of liquid waste.

clue.text: Bank allowance limits to stop

indicators.note: to limit is to bound or enclose, so the allowance holds the stop within it

parts.note: a grant is a sum allowed or awarded
to die is to stop, as an engine dies

explanation.surface: A bank that caps an allowance to stop it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money, and allowance plays along, but it means a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank is a sloping piece of ground, and a slope is a gradient.

clue.text: NASA's last head initially opted for lunar mission

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the space agency's name

parts.note: poll is an old word for the head, as in poll tax

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The head of NASA decides on a moon programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not NASA's chief but POLL, an old word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The US space programme that landed astronauts on the Moon was named after the Greek god.

clue.text: Eye Troy in old image

indicators.note: in puts the weight abbreviation inside the word for image

parts.note: pic is short for picture, an image
t is the abbreviation for troy, the system of weights for precious metals

explanation.surface: Studying Troy in an ancient picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troy' is not the city but troy weight, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is a jocular or technical word for the eye, the organ of sight.

clue.text: Dis the criminal fraternity

definitions.meaning: Dis is the Roman god of the dead and his realm, Hades
organised crime and its members collectively, gangland

explanation.surface: Slang 'dis' as insulting the mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dis' reads as slang for disrespect, but it is the Roman god of the dead and his kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The realm of the dead in myth and the world of organised crime share this one name.

clue.text: Draw Roger opening note

indicators.note: opening means splitting open, so the note is cut by the other word

parts.note: te is the seventh note in tonic sol-fa
Roger in radio talk means message received, okay

explanation.surface: A man named Roger draws the first note in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger' is not a name but the radio acknowledgement meaning OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag on a cannabis cigarette is a draw on it, slang for a puff.

clue.text: Ancient mariner goes in for each song book

indicators.note: goes in means the sailor is put inside the following word

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per person'
an old salt is a veteran sailor

explanation.surface: Coleridge's old seaman takes up hymn books for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient mariner' evokes Coleridge's poem, but it is just SALT, an old sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalter is a book of the Psalms, songs used in worship.

clue.text: A Romeo longing to hug new colleague here

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: to hug is to hold within the arms, so the longing encloses the new

parts.note: an ache is a longing, as in to ache for

explanation.surface: A lover longs to embrace a new workmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colleague here' refers to Crucible's fellow Guardian setter Arachne.
explanation.definitionFit: Arachne, named after the weaver turned into a spider, sets cryptic puzzles for the same newspaper as this setter.
